newsitem.title: USA: OPTIONS - Dlr/yen volatility rises on spot slide.
newsitem.headline: OPTIONS - Dlr/yen volatility rises on spot slide.

text.p: Implied volatilities on dollar/yen options rose in U.S. trading Tuesday after the dollar gave up ground against the yen overnight.
Volatility began to climb during the European morning as demand for spot yen picked up.
"People are starting to look at the downside again" in dollar/yen, said an options trader for a Japanese bank in New York.
Traders said the focus remained on buying yen calls in shorter-term durations.
Sizable corporate interest was seen in three-month 15-delta yen calls in the 118.00 strike this morning.

While many in the foreign exchange market look for the dollar to bounce off 125.00 yen and stay in a range defined by 130.00 on the upside over the next few months, an equal number see dollar/yen's trading band downshifting, the Japanese bank trader said. The trader suggested a new range for dollar/yen could span 122.00 to 127.00.

Volatility pushed higher amid the mixed sentiment. In the U.S., one-month dollar/yen at midday had climbed to 8.50/8.75 percent from 8.20/8.30 Monday. One-year was quoted at 9.35/9.65 percent, up from 9.20/9.30.
The dollar was bid at 125.30 yen, near the European low.
One-month 25-delta risk reversals widened their yen call skew to 0.3/0.7. Risk reversals measure the pricing differential between puts and calls.
In dollar/mark, volatility edged lower along with the spot, with long-term sentiment still favoring a strengthening of the dollar versus European currencies, traders said.
Risk reversals were flat/0.4 bid for mark puts.
One-month dollar/mark implied volatility was 8.40/8.60 percent, down 0.1 point from Monday. One-year was virtually steady at 9.15/9.20 percent.
"The offer side of the curve is stocked with supply," said an options trader for a European bank.
Traders said it would take a move in dollar/mark above 1.7400 to ignite volatility.
Cable volatilities jumped following a quarter-point rise in British base rates to 6.25 percent and news the Bank of England is to gain operational independence to set rates.
One-week sterling/dollar volatility jumped 1.0 point from Monday's levels, while one-year rose 0.2 point to 7.55/7.85 percent.
The European bank trader said the market would wait to see if the spot could maintain this morning's advance above 1.6300.
